blocks.raw: <ExamTip>When an LEA question presents a structural scenario, mentally walk the load path before selecting an answer. Ask: where does the load originate? How does it travel to the ground? What material and system is carrying it? This chain-of-reasoning approach catches the most common trap answers, which are correct for a different point in the chain.</ExamTip>

blocks.raw: <ElaborativeInterrogation question="Why can a building that is adequate for gravity loads still be structurally deficient under seismic loads?" answer="Gravity load design optimizes for vertical force paths — columns, beams, slabs carrying weight downward. Seismic loads are horizontal and cyclic, creating lateral story forces, overturning moments, and torsional demands that gravity systems are not configured to resist. A building without shear walls, moment frames, or braced frames has no dedicated lateral system and will rack — potentially collapsing — under significant seismic demand. This is why NSCP Chapter 2 requires a complete lateral force-resisting system independent of gravity considerations." />

props.question: Why can a building that is adequate for gravity loads still be structurally deficient under seismic loads?
props.answer: Gravity load design optimizes for vertical force paths — columns, beams, slabs carrying weight downward. Seismic loads are horizontal and cyclic, creating lateral story forces, overturning moments, and torsional demands that gravity systems are not configured to resist. A building without shear walls, moment frames, or braced frames has no dedicated lateral system and will rack — potentially collapsing — under significant seismic demand. This is why NSCP Chapter 2 requires a complete lateral force-resisting system independent of gravity considerations.

blocks.raw: <Tip>When you encounter an unfamiliar exam question in this subject, trace the load path. Start with the load type (gravity? lateral? seismic?), identify where it enters the structure, follow it through the structural system, and end at the foundation. The answer usually reveals itself somewhere along that path.</Tip>
